questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not have a lot of specific requests considering the destination, but I found that McMaster had a lot of interesting elective courses that the University of Copenhagen doesn't offer. I also thought that Canada was an interesting destination to explore so this was a plus for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hamilton is not the most charming city in Canada. It is close to Toronto, which made it easy to go on day trips and to travel around in Canada, but Hamilton city itself does not have a lot to offer. McMaster University has a very big campus, with a lot of activities going on all the time, which was fun to experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found that McMaster had a lot of information and considering that it is a very big University I found that it worked pretty well. The first orientation however was a lot of practical information, and it needed more activities where we got to interact with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a correspondence with an academic advisor from McMaster, which worked well. However I struggled with gaining access to a mandatory course, which was quite stressful and I found that this issue could have been solved very quickly (because it seemed like it was only a technical issue that prevented me from taking the course)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: McMaster has something called student success center, where most of the practical information can be found. They even have a medical practice on campus (which is included in the health insurance that is mandatory).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing market in Hamilton is really bad. The prices are terrible for what you can get and from what i gathered from people living on campus is that this option is really expensive as well (and the dorms are in bad shape + it is mandatory to buy a meal plan). I managed to find an airbnb with some other exchange students from KU that had a reasonable rent, however it was 30-40 min away from campus and the house itself was not the best.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Look for housing in advance since the market is really bad, and maybe see if you can track down a whatsapp group (or a facebook group - I used KU-studerende i Canada) to get in touch with other people who are going on exchange or even students who are currently on exchange whose housing will be available once they leave. Also beware that there's a lot of housing scams, so be sure that the housing you find is legit.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was also really grateful for being able to live with some of the other danish students, because for me this meant that I had a very safe base at home. That being said, I know that a lot of people who lived on campus made a lot of friends (many of these were other exchange students), so this option is very nice if you want to live with other students and get to know people this way.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McMaster offers a lot of courses so it is a bit difficult to get the broad overview of everything they offer, since the list of courses sometimes are divided in the different faculties. I discovered some new courses once I arrived that I had not seen beforehand.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I first had to submit my prerequisites for the courses that I was planning on taking at McMaster. These had to be approved before I was allowed to enroll in any courses. The system for selecting courses worked quite well, because you had an opportunity to see all of the possible schedules and select the ones that were most convenient for you. The first week of school is meant for you to try out different courses and make your final selection, but the courses gets filled up so make sure that you enroll in the ones you are most interested in, because you have a lot of time to drop the courses again.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mostly contacted my academic advisor whenever I had issues with the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get the courses I wanted, even after some issues with the enrollment in one of my mandatory courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When I had an issue with one of my courses I scheduled a meeting with my academic advisor and she was able to fix it - so seek all of the help that you need, and try to not stress too much about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McMaster have midterms during the semester and your assignments throughout the semester all count towards your final grade.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level at McMaster is quite low compared to KU and they use a lot of multiple choice exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses had tutorials, but most of my courses were only had lectures. I found that people were very open, so even if a course did not have a tutorial, there was still an opportunity to work with other students in the courses that only had lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HLTHAGE 1CC3: Introduction to Mental Health and Illness
ANTHROP 1AB3:Introduction to Anthropology: Race, Religion, and Social Justice
PSYCH 2AP3: Abnormal Psychology: Fundamentals and Major Disorders 
GENDRST 2AA3: Feminist Thought

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
HLTHAGE 1CC3: Introduction to Mental Health and Illness - I took this course because I needed to to cover "klinisk psykologi" at KU. It turned out to be a really good course, because I found that the professor is very good and he has a quite critical approach to the subject of mental health which I thought was interesting. This course focuses on writing skills rather than memorizing multiple choice questions - but it is a first-year course, so the requirements are not very strict for these compared to KU. 

ANTHROP 1AB3:Introduction to Anthropology: Race, Religion, and Social Justice - This was one of my electives and I was really happy about this course as well. It is also a first-year course so in the beginning there was a lot of basic stuff that I found to be a bit tiresome, but once the introductory part was over I really enjoyed the perspectives that this course gave me. The instructor is really good and I like the fact that he also empathizes the fact that memorizing small details does not make sense - but gaining an overall understanding of the course is much more important. 

PSYCH 2AP3: Abnormal Psychology: Fundamentals and Major Disorders - I also had to take this course to cover the other part of "klinisk". This course was a disappointments, because it consisted of memorizing a lot of information to be tested on 3 multiple choice exams in total. It had a very narrow-minded approach to the subject of mental health, so I can only recommend taking this course if it's absolutely necessary (which it might be if you're a psychology student, because KU was really strict with approving my courses for klinisk)

GENDRST 2AA3: Feminist Thought - This course was an elective and I really enjoyed it. Throughout the semester I had to write journal entries about the course content which made me engage with the material in another way than I otherwise would have. I also had to so a creative assignment and write a feminist manifest which I found to be a really nice experience (to get to submit assignments that are different from what I'm normally used to). I also think that this course had a big impact on the way I see the world, so it had a personal impact for me as well. The professor in this course is very good as well, so if you're interested in learning more about feminism I can really recommend this course!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was mandatory to pay for health insurance through the university.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The phone subscription in Canada was more expensive than I expected (I used Freedom mobile and had one of their cheapest subscriptions with 10 GB per month - this only worked in Ontario and I even experienced that when I travelled inside Ontario, this was quite unreliable still). 

There are some food items that are more expensive compared to Denmark (meat, cheese and some vegetables) - however other food items are cheaper (such as eggs and other kinds of vegetables), so it evens out. 

It is quite expensive to travel inside Canada, and I did a lot of small trips, which is why I put approximately 5000 DKK for other fees (this is hostel/airbnb, transport and food).

I spent more money on having dinner at restaurants than I usually do at home, but this is because prices are cheaper for this in Canada (this can be done for about 85-140 DKK for a whole meal + water is free everywhere you eat out)

A plus was that fact that buses in Hamilton were free if you're a student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McMaster has so many clubs and activities that you can join whether you're into sports, outdoor tours or creative things.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many clubs available for everything - you can probably find a list of the one currently available if you search for it, but otherwise they had 2 days where all of the clubs came to promote themselves where you could join if you were interested.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: McMaster has an outdoor club which organises trips throughout the semester - I joined a canoe trip to Algonquin park and I can really recommend doing this! It's a nice way to mingle with other students, both exchange and canadian students, and if you're there during the fall terms, the autumn colors are so beautiful at this time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I took weekend trips to Quebec, New York, Bruce Peninsula park and Vancouver during the semester and I found that this was totally manageable because the academic level was not very overwhelming. Also taking day trips to Toronto from Hamilton with the go bus is a nice idea.
I also travelled before my semester started and I can recommend visiting Ottawa and Montreal .

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: This was quite easy since Canadians are very welcoming in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to approach people at lectures, most people are very friendly and don't find it odd. Also, join some clubs to get to know the locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They use cars for everything, so sometimes this limited the opportunities to travel different places.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are so friendly and easy to approach and this made me appreciate Canada even more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid to socialize with people - both other exchange students and locals. 
Make sure to check out all of the courses that McMaster offers, because they have so many unique and special courses that I don't think you'll be able to try out (as electives) back home. 
Go on some of the outdoor trips!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The fall semester ends in december (the latest exams are held on the 22), so this gives a good opportunity to travel a bit before going back to DK (I went to Mexico for 3 weeks after my final exams).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to travel and experience a lot of things that I wouldn't otherwise would do during a semester. Also trying out some courses that were very different from what I normally would study was very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was quite stressed when I arrived because my courses did not seem to work out, so it was a bit of a rough start having to communicate both with McMaster and KU trying to figure it out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I was on exchange during my 5. semester, so I tried to find courses that corresponded with "klinisk psykologi", "psykiatri" and "videnskabsteori og forskningsdesign". In line with the challenge of getting my courses to work out, I found that I had very limited options when I tried to get my courses to approved from KU - I ended up only having two options for courses that KU would approve as "klinisk" (1 course at McMaster correlates with 7,5 ects), which meant that I really had to make sure to get these courses. 
I was also not able to take "psykiatri "(so I ended up being enrolled in the KU course during the semester and taking the re-exam once I got back) and furthermore I could not get approval for any courses corresponding to "videnskabsteori og forskningsdesign" which is why I ended up using my electives during the exchange.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
